papers.title: The S-technique: A Novel Dense Polytetrafluoroethylene-assisted Surgical Technique for Peri-implant Keratinized Mucosa Preservation - A Case Review.
papers.abstract: Immediate implant placement following tooth extraction often leads to peri-implant defects that require guided bone regeneration (GBR) to achieve complete bone fill and stable osseointegration. Conventional GBR techniques typically rely on primary flap closure, coronal advancement, and additional soft-tissue grafting, which increase surgical complexity and patient morbidity. The S-Technique was introduced to enable simultaneous hard and soft-tissue regeneration under open-healing conditions while preserving the mucogingival junction. A patient presented with a grossly decayed, painful, vertically fractured, nonrestorable maxillary right second premolar (tooth 15). After atraumatic extraction and immediate implant placement, a peri-implant gap defect with limited soft-tissue availability was noted. GBR was performed using particulate xenograft and a resorbable collagen membrane. A dense polytetrafluoroethylene membrane was then placed according to the S-technique protocol, allowing secondary epithelialization without primary closure. Healing progressed uneventfully. At 4 months, clinical assessment showed complete coverage of the peri-implant site, an adequate band of keratinized mucosa, improved soft-tissue contour, a favorable emergence profile, and stable peri-implant architecture. Prosthetic rehabilitation resulted in satisfactory esthetic and functional outcomes with maintained bone support. This case demonstrates the S-Technique as a minimally invasive dual-layer membrane approach for simultaneous hard and soft-tissue regeneration around immediate implants. By eliminating the need for primary closure and autogenous soft-tissue grafting, it offers a predictable alternative for managing peri-implant defects in sites with limited soft-tissue availability, while promoting keratinized mucosa formation and stable peri-implant tissue integration.

summary_en.motivation: Immediate implant placement frequently creates peri-implant defects that conventionally require flap closure and soft-tissue grafting, increasing morbidity.
summary_en.method: A dense polytetrafluoroethylene membrane was applied in an S-technique configuration over a xenograft and collagen membrane to permit open-healing hard and soft tissue regeneration.

papers.title: Managing the Noise: Harnessing the Power of Graph Neural Networks to Detect Subsurface Damage under Noisy Experimental Settings
papers.abstract: Abstract Aging infrastructure with limited budgets has driven stakeholders to explore new methods for monitoring structural health. Structural health monitoring represents a strategy to address this challenge using physical measurements to characterize performance. This approach has often leveraged various sensing modalities to describe operational response to loading environment, with most strategies relying on continuous measurement. In recent years, the complexity and economic constraints associated with continuous monitoring have motivated alternatives. The digital twin framework offers a model-first approach, where real-world data informs virtual models (the “twin”), enables dynamic updates based on measurements and further offers enhanced assessment and predictive capabilities. This work formulates a graph neural network-powered prototype digital twin of a structural system that can identify unseen damage through updating intact finite element models of small-scale representations of structural elements based on full-field measurements. Within this study, MeshGraphNet is trained on noisy strain and displacement data using noise statistics characterized from a physical digital image correlation experimental setup, which differs from most existing methods that rely on idealized or synthetically generated noise. Three models were trained on noise-free data, data with noise, and data with improved signal-to-noise ratios. Results demonstrate that model performance correlates positively with damage severity, achieving an F1 score of 43.79% for the damaged class across the data set. Performance improved substantially when evaluated on specific damage severity ranges, reaching 78.75% for instances with 45%–50% damage, as shear strain exceeds the noise floor at higher damage severities. When compared to robust principal component analysis and denoising autoencoders, the proposed mixed data training strategy outperforms these preprocessing methods. Validation on a physical dogbone specimen demonstrates consistent performance across simulated and experimental data, indicating potential for real-world implementation. Future work aims to extend the framework to more extensive experimental data and assess the scalability of the trained model for larger and more complex structural systems.

papers.title: Decoding the Impact of Solvent Hydrogen-Bonding Networks on Nanozyme Activity via Machine Learning Potentials
papers.abstract: Precise mechanistic insights into the chemical reactions at solid-liquid interfaces are crucial for advancing functional nanomaterials, such as enzyme-mimicking nanocatalysts known as nanozymes. However, conventional periodic density functional theory (DFT) calculations, usually performed under vacuum conditions, can systematically underestimate reaction barriers, leading to discrepancies between computational predictions and the catalytic performance of nanomaterials in aqueous environments. Here, we propose a deep potential (DP)-based strategy that integrates DFT, ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and active learning to resolve solvent-mediated reaction kinetics. Using hydrogen peroxide dissociation on Au(111) as a prototypical model reaction for nanozyme activity, we develop a DP model that show comparable accuracy to DFT calculations, enabling efficient identification of transition states in explicit solvents. Calculations using this model have demonstrated that the aqueous hydrogen-bonding network significantly increases the energy barrier for $H_2O_2$ dissociation by 0.58 eV, the experimentally observed low activity of gold nanoparticles in aqueous media. This approach provides a robust framework to decode solvent effects on chemical reactions at solid-liquid interfaces, which is valuable for advancing the rational design of functional nanocatalysts such as nanozymes.

papers.title: Optimization of an Explainable Machine Learning Model for Customer Churn Prediction and Business Retention Strategy
papers.abstract: Customer churn forecasting is critical for companies that want to identify potential churn customers and develop more targeted customer maintenance strategies. This study explores whether Bayesian optimization can improve the performance of machine learning in customer churn prediction, and whether explainable model output can provide useful business insights. This research used Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) to analyze the IBM Telecom customer churn data set containing 7,043 customer records. We applied Bayesian hyperparameter optimization to XGBoost by using five-fold hierarchical cross-validation, and used SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to explain the optimized model. The optimized XGBoost model achieves the Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.8424 and the Precision-Recall Area Under the Curve (PR-AUC) of 0.6518, and the recall rate also increased from 0.6408 in the baseline XGBoost model to 0.7721. SHAP analysis shows that the type of contract, user duration and Internet services are the most influential predictors. Risk segmentation further shows that there are significant differences in the churn rates of different customer groups. Research results show that combining model optimization with interpretable analysis helps to make more transparent and targeted customer retention decisions.
papers.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
